config.title: Promises & Async/Await

intro.title: Promises & Async/Await
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that simulates fetching data from a server using JavaScript's Promise and async/await syntax. You'll learn how to handle asynchronous operations, which are tasks like reading files or making network requests that take time to complete. The core concepts covered include creating Promises, using .then() and .catch() for handling results and errors, and writing cleaner code with async functions and the await keyword. By the end, you'll understand how to manage delayed tasks in JavaScript without blocking your program's execution.
intro.usecase: Promises and async/await are essential for handling asynchronous operations in modern web applications. You'll use them when fetching data from APIs to populate dashboards with real-time metrics, submitting form data without page reloads, or loading user profiles and content dynamically. These patterns ensure smooth user experiences in features like live search filters, infinite scrolling feeds, and interactive data visualizations that update without blocking the UI.

objectives: Construct a Promise object to handle asynchronous operations
Apply .then() and .catch() methods to process Promise resolutions and rejections
Implement async functions to write asynchronous code with synchronous-like syntax
Manipulate multiple Promises using Promise.all() for concurrent execution
Initialize error handling within async/await patterns using try...catch blocks
Integrate Promise-based APIs with async/await to fetch and process data

steps.title: Create a promise that resolves with a success message
steps.instruction: Create a new Promise object that resolves with the string 'Operation successful!' after a 1-second delay using setTimeout.
steps.hint: Remember to use the Promise constructor, which takes a function with resolve and reject parameters. Inside that function, use setTimeout to delay the resolve call.
steps.seedCode: // Create a new Promise that resolves with 'Operation successful!' after 1 second
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a Promise object that resolves with the success message after the specified delay.
successCriteria: A Promise is created with setTimeout inside, calling resolve('Operation successful!') after 1000 milliseconds.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your Promise uses setTimeout to delay the resolve call by 1000 milliseconds.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a new Promise with a function that uses setTimeout to resolve with 'Operation successful!' after 1 second.

steps.title: Handle the resolved promise with .then()
steps.instruction: Chain a .then() method to your promise to log the resolved value to the console.
steps.hint: The .then() method takes a callback function that receives the resolved value as its argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The promise will resolve after 1 second and log 'Operation successful!' to the console.
successCriteria: The promise has a .then() method attached that logs the resolved value to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your .then() callback logs the resolved value to console.
steps.feedbackWrong: The promise needs a .then() method that logs the resolved value. Check the syntax.

steps.title: Create a promise that rejects with an error
steps.instruction: Create a new Promise named errorPromise that rejects with an Error object containing the message 'Something went wrong!' after a 1-second delay using setTimeout.
steps.hint: Use the Promise constructor with both resolve and reject parameters. Call reject() with new Error('Something went wrong!') inside setTimeout.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new promise named errorPromise that will reject with an Error after 1 second.
successCriteria: The errorPromise is defined using new Promise with reject called inside setTimeout, passing new Error('Something went wrong!').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the reject function inside setTimeout and passing an Error object with the correct message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The promise isn't set up to reject properly. Remember to use the reject parameter in the Promise constructor and call it with new Error('Something went wrong!') inside setTimeout.

steps.title: Handle the rejected promise with .catch()
steps.instruction: Chain a .catch() method to the errorPromise to log the error message to the console.
steps.hint: After the promise definition, add .catch(error => console.log(error)) to handle any rejection.
steps.expectedOutcome: The errorPromise will reject with 'Operation failed!' and the .catch() will log that message to the console.
successCriteria: errorPromise has a .catch() method attached that logs the error message to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've attached .catch() to errorPromise and it logs the error message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The promise rejection isn't being handled. Remember to chain .catch() to errorPromise and log the error inside it.

steps.title: Create an async function that returns a resolved value
steps.instruction: Create an async function called fetchData that returns the string 'Data loaded successfully'.
steps.hint: Use the async keyword before the function declaration or arrow function, then return the string directly.
steps.expectedOutcome: An async function named fetchData is created that returns the string 'Data loaded successfully'.
successCriteria: The async function fetchData is declared and returns the exact string 'Data loaded successfully'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is declared with the async keyword and returns the exact string 'Data loaded successfully'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create an async function named fetchData that returns the string 'Data loaded successfully'.

steps.title: Call the async function and handle its result with .then()
steps.instruction: Call the fetchData function and chain a .then() method to log the returned value to the console.
steps.hint: Since fetchData is an async function, it returns a promise. You can use .then() on that promise to access its resolved value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The async function fetchData is called, and its returned promise is handled with .then() to log the resolved value.
successCriteria: .then() method is chained to the call
console.log is used inside .then() to log the value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling fetchData() and chaining .then() with console.log inside to handle the resolved value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember that async functions return promises, so you need to call fetchData() and use .then() to access and log the value it resolves with.

steps.title: Handle errors in async functions with try/catch
steps.instruction: Create an async function called safeFetch that uses try/catch to handle a promise rejection and returns an error message.
steps.hint: Define an async function named safeFetch. Inside, use try/catch to await a promise that rejects, and return the error message from the catch block.

steps.title: Chain multiple async operations with await
steps.instruction: Create an async function called sequentialTasks that awaits two separate promises in sequence and returns their combined results.
steps.hint: Define an async function named sequentialTasks. Inside, use await to wait for the first promise, then the second, and return a string combining both results.
steps.expectedOutcome: An async function named sequentialTasks is defined, which uses two await statements to wait for promises sequentially and returns their combined results.
successCriteria: The code includes an async function named sequentialTasks that uses two await statements and returns a combined string of the awaited values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your sequentialTasks function is async, uses two await statements, and returns a combined result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Remember to create an async function named sequentialTasks that awaits two promises and returns their combined results.

steps.title: Run parallel async operations with Promise.all
steps.instruction: Create an async function called parallelTasks that uses Promise.all to await multiple promises simultaneously and returns their results.
steps.hint: Define an async function named parallelTasks. Inside, use Promise.all() with an array of promises, await it, and return the result.
steps.expectedOutcome: An async function named parallelTasks is defined that uses Promise.all to handle multiple promises concurrently.
successCriteria: The parallelTasks function is defined as async, uses Promise.all with an array of promises, awaits it, and returns the results.
